curriculum.subject: Mathematical Activities
curriculum.outcomeText: compare the capacity of two containers using more than, less than, and same as

mission.title: compare the capacity of two containers using more than, less than, and same as

interactions.prompt: Two cups are filled to the top. Which cup holds more water?
interactions.feedback: Yes! The large cup holds more water.
interactions.retryHint: Imagine filling both cups to the top. Which one has more space inside?

interactions.prompt: Watch the fill marks. The jug takes 4 small cups. The bowl takes 2 small cups. Which holds less?

model.comparison: The jug needs 4 equal small cups. The bowl needs 2 equal small cups.

interactions.feedback: Correct! The bowl holds less because it takes fewer small cups.
interactions.retryHint: Look for the container with the smaller number of equal cups.

interactions.prompt: Match the words to the containers. The bucket holds more than the cup.
interactions.tapAlternative: Tap a container, then tap its matching words.
interactions.feedback: Great matching! The bucket holds more and the cup holds less.
interactions.retryHint: Start with the bigger container. It has more space inside.

interactions.prompt: A tea flask and a water bottle each take 3 equal cups to fill. They hold...
interactions.feedback: Well done! Both containers hold the same as each other.
interactions.retryHint: Both containers take the same number of equal cups.

interactions.prompt: At the school garden, match each container to the right comparison with the watering can. The watering can takes 5 equal cups.
interactions.tapAlternative: Tap a container, then tap the comparison that fits it.
interactions.feedback: Excellent! You compared each container with the watering can.
interactions.retryHint: Compare each number with 5: smaller means less, bigger means more, and 5 means the same.

interactions.prompt: Show what you know. Which statement is true? A basin takes 6 equal cups. A jug takes 4 equal cups.
choices: The basin holds more than the jug.
The basin holds less than the jug.
The basin holds the same as the jug.
interactions.answer: The basin holds more than the jug.
interactions.feedback: Well done! Six cups is more than four cups, so the basin holds more.
interactions.retryHint: Compare 6 and 4. The container needing more equal cups holds more.
